rubric:
VERIFIED from the official Rules (rulesContent at https://builder.aws.com/build/hackathons/e83e84e5-4f4c-383b-bbe9-4a15ac195d55/zero-to-shipped?tab=rules) and the official FAQ (https://builder.aws.com/content/3JVxSt0eLCUFivz63h9RFbQtmLv/zero-to-shipped-faqs):

0) SHIP GATE (pass/fail, no exceptions)
- The app must be live on AWS and reachable at a public URL at the time of evaluation, which runs through the weeks of Oct 5 and Oct 12.
- The project must include documented proof of the coding agent's connection to the AWS console.
- It must be accessible to both the AI scoring system and the human judges.
- Anything not live does not advance.

1) GATE 1, week of Oct 5: "AI Scoring and Human Review". All qualifying submissions are scored by a combination of AI and human review:
- Technical Innovation & Originality: 25%
- Implementation Quality: 25%
- Community/Market Impact: 25%
- Creativity & Storytelling: 25%
The top 100 by composite score advance.

2) GATE 2, week of Oct 12: human judging by "a panel of AWS experts and community leaders" on the same four criteria at 25% each. They select 5 winners "across the app categories". Winners are announced the week of Oct 19, after eligibility verification.

DISCREPANCY: The About tab calls Round 1 plain "AI scoring" on "creativity and storytelling, technical innovation, community and market impact, and communication quality". That list has no weights and no top-N, names "communication quality" instead of "Implementation Quality", and omits "Originality". The Rules and FAQ, which are authoritative, use the four 25% criteria above.

AI SCORER: Not defined publicly. There is no model name, no vendor and no description of its inputs. The only statement is that the app must be "publicly reachable by judges and the AI scoring system". INFERRED: it most likely reads the published Builder Center project (title, 512-character description, markdown body, tags, links) and fetches the live URL. So the landing page should serve meaningful HTML without login or JS-only rendering, and the write-up should address each criterion explicitly.

Other scoring-relevant rules:
- Tags route the project for scoring: one category tag and one lane tag, with the lane tag written "startups" (confirmed by the organizer) or "community".
- A GitHub repo is optional but "could help judges".
- If an entry reuses architecture from prior work, include an architecture comparison diagram (organizer guidance).
- No bonus criteria are published anywhere.

proof:
VERIFIED: - The Rules require "documented proof of coding agent connection to the AWS console", and the agent must be connected "before or during the Submission Period". The proof goes inside the published Builder Center project. - The organizer, Ben Fowler (AWS), replied in Discussion: "The rules require documented proof of your coding agent connection to the AWS console, but don't specify an exact format. So, make it as clear and verifiable as possible: screenshots, logs, or a short walkthrough that shows the connection in action are all reasonable approaches. As for region, the rules don't specify or restrict which AWS region you use." - The FAQ links the official method: "Connect your AI coding agent to AWS" by Ana Cunha, AWS Developer Advocate (https://builder.aws.com/content/3JQdUYne1ujIvtoLgWiV7iBGklF/connect-your-ai-coding-agent-to-aws). It uses the Agent Toolkit for AWS, meaning the AWS MCP Server plus skills: - Either click "Get setup prompt" on the AWS Console Home banner and paste it into the agent, - or do it manually: AWS CLI 2.35.0 or later, then `aws login`, then `aws configure agent-toolkit`, then restart the agent. - Verify by asking the agent "What AWS Regions are available?" - For Claude Code, the official setup doc (https://github.com/aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws/blob/main/setup-instructions/setup.md) is: `aws login --region --profile

`, then `aws configure agent-toolkit --yes --region us-east-1 --profile

`, then set `AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES` in the Claude Code MCP config. - AWS docs say the MCP server adds the IAM context keys `aws:ViaAWSMCPService` and `aws:CalledViaAWSMCP` to every request, and "CloudTrail logs all API calls for audit visibility" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/what-is-agent-toolkit.html). - Risk: one participant's Kiro screenshot was rejected by Builder Center's image moderation as "inappropriate content". Keep a text version of the proof as well. INFERRED best practice, based on the strongest competitor write-ups (ShiftGuard, AgentSentry AI, Firsthand): 1. The MCP config snippet as a code block: the aws-mcp entry pointing to https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp. 2. The output of `aws configure agent-toolkit`. 3. Agent-issued calls through MCP, such as `sts get-caller-identity` and a get/describe on a deployed resource, with request IDs and timestamps, and the account ID partly masked. 4. A CloudTrail Event history screenshot filtered to the agent's session or role, showing the MCP-originated calls. 5. Optionally a dedicated least-privilege IAM role or profile for the agent. 6. Optionally a 1 to 2 minute walkthrough video. 7. A "how the agent helped" section tying agent actions to shipped resources. Also mirror the evidence on an /evidence page of the live app so both the judges and the AI scorer can reach it.
submission_fields:
VERIFIED sources: Builder Center FAQ (https://builder.aws.com/faq#hackathons), the "Introducing Hackathons" article (https://builder.aws.com/content/3JVlS5EVmqlZEcNMWMNeJhln9Sp/introducing-hackathons-on-aws-builder-center) and the submissions API schema.

A submission is a Builder Center project created on the hackathon's "Your project" tab after joining. Publishing the project is what submits it.

Form fields:
- Title: up to 255 characters.
- Description: up to 512 characters, "one or two sentences … without repeating the title".
- Body: rich text with headings, bold, italic, inline code, code blocks, links, bulleted and numbered lists, images, dividers and tables.
- Cover image: optional, recommended 1200x675, max 2 MB, jpg/png/webp, text in images not recommended.
- Tags: max 5. Two are required: one category tag (#workplace-efficiency / #daily-life-enhancement / #commercial-potential / #social-good / #personal-expression) and one lane tag (#startups / #community).
- GitHub or GitLab repository link: optional.
- Endpoint or live demo link: optional as a field, but the rules require the live URL in the project.
- Jupyter or SageMaker notebook link: optional.
- The API object fields are title, description, markdownDescription, heroImageUrl, tags, githubLink, liveDemoLink and sageMakerLink.

Content the Rules require inside the project:
- (a) proof of the coding agent connection
- (b) a description of the project and the development process
- (c) the app category and focus track
- (d) a link to the live application
- documentation of the AWS services and coding agent used
- About tab wording: "how the coding agent helped you ship"

Mechanics:
- Up to 5 team members (the leader plus 4 invited builders who have Builder IDs and have joined). Solo entries are allowed.
- One project per builder per hackathon, and "Limit one entry per person".
- Only the team leader can edit.
- The project stays editable until Oct 2, 11:59 PM PDT. After that everything freezes, and an unpublished draft can never be published or win.
- Posts in the Discussion tab are NOT submissions; the organizer has redirected several people who posted there.
unknowns:
NOT FOUND or NOT PUBLISHED (searched: the hackathon page, the embedded JSON, the Rules, the FAQ article, the Builder Center FAQ, all 42 Discussion posts and their comments, and web search):

1. The AI scoring system: no model or vendor is named, and there is no description of what it reads or how it treats the live URL, JS-only pages, GitHub repos or videos. It is also unknown how AI and human scores combine in Gate 1, and who the Gate 1 human reviewers are.
2. The rubric conflict: the About tab lists "communication quality" and leaves out Implementation Quality. The Rules and FAQ, which are authoritative, list four criteria at 25% each. There are no sub-criteria or score scales.
3. "Community leaders" on the Gate 2 panel are not named. The sidebar lists only 5 AWS-staff judges.
4. "5 winners across the app categories" is not defined as one per category. It is also unknown whether lanes affect scoring or winner allocation beyond routing.
5. No bonus criteria were found: nothing extra for a particular agent (Kiro, Q), for particular AWS services, for videos, or for likes and comments. Likes are visible, but there is no statement that they count.
6. There is no exact proof format. The organizer said any clear, verifiable format is fine and that region is unrestricted.
7. How long after Oct 12 the app must stay live is not stated. The finalist eligibility checks and the Oct 19 announcement suggest keeping it up longer.
8. The Social Impact Credits eligibility criteria on pulse.amazon were not fetched in detail.
9. The Participants and "Your project" tabs need sign-in and were not accessed.
10. No separate PDF of the official rules exists. The Rules tab text is the Terms and Conditions (last updated Sep 18, 2026).
11. The tab parameters about, rules, judges, prizes, resources, faq, updates, discussions, participants, submissions, gallery, schedule and overview all serve the same page. Only About, Your project, Projects, Discussion, Participants and Rules exist, plus Winners after winners are declared.
12. The hackathon listing page (https://builder.aws.com/build/hackathons) loads its list client-side, and the list was not extracted. It adds nothing specific to this event.
13. Whether AWS-hosted custom domains are accepted is not stated. INFERRED: fine, if the app runs on AWS.

INFERRED, not verified: Vercel, Render, GitHub Pages or Streamlit hosting likely fails "live on AWS". Of the 150 published projects, 35 have no live link and about 44 have links outside AWS domains (some of those custom domains may still be on AWS).
